unique_original_proof: Write initial square vertices P=(0,0),R=(s,0),S=(s,s),T=(0,s), with s=10. Successive clockwise90-degree rolls pivot about R=(s,0), then S=(2s,0), then T=(3s,0). The tracked P positions after these turns are(s,s),(3s,s),(4s,0). Its successive distances to the actual pivots are s,s*sqrt(2),s. P stays above the line between its departure and the end of the third turn, so first return occurs then. The length is(pi/2)*(s+s*sqrt(2)+s)=10pi+5pi*sqrt(2), uniquely C. The subsequent turn about P contributes zero but is outside the first-return path. The native diagram deliberately shows only45-degree portions of the first/last arcs and compresses the intervening motion by an ellipsis; these are not the entire measured path. In all three displayed square poses the same material side P-R is respectively initial bottom edge, dashed tilted P-to-pivot edge, and terminal right edge. These correspondences preserve material identity.
